scope: Read-only source review of BLOOM conversion metadata, alias/QKV transformation ordering, tokenizer class branches and complete-file/regression tests. No tests or conversions were executed by this reviewer.
checks: Frozen BloomModel metadata override preserves hidden_size/n_embed and n_head/num_attention_heads precedence, emits fixed four-times-hidden FFN width, required epsilon and original file type.

Resolved BloomConfig consumes non-null n_embed, hides consumed/aliased keys in normalized root serialization, and permits inherited aliases to overwrite initialized n_head/n_layer; this matches inspected Transformers4.57.6 source.
All literal transformer. segments are removed after contribution dictionary semantics, preserving collisions for canonical publication checks.

Fused QKV transform acts on source head-major blocks and checked original element counts; weight and bias zero/nondivisible cases preserve their distinct source behavior. Empty permutation buffers terminate before iterating large head counts.
New head-count sequence serialization uses original GGUF element wire kinds and a declared recursion bound; malformed and heterogeneous cases fail explicitly.

BloomTokenizerFast default specials and truthy recursive ByteLevel prefix update match inspected installed source and retained native class corpus. Existing other tokenizer family guard remains separate.

Complete-file test pins input blob data, independent original output hashes and retained failure statuses; budget test requires failure before publishing over an existing destination and checks temporary-file cleanup.
Pretrained test verifies unchanged official input hashes before/after conversion, uses a fresh output root, and compares all three complete original output hashes and byte counts.
limitations: Review is limited to the sampled identities; later implementation changes require refresh.
No blanket assurance for untested architectures or tokenizer backends; no repository-wide release gate is closed.
The reviewer has inspected source and test contracts, while actual test execution remains the owning agent's validation.
